transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Yes, we can help. A Dyson that keeps pulsing even with a full battery is very often something you can sort at home without a repair. This sounds like normal behaviour rather than a fault: A cordless vacuum pulsing on and off is its warning that airflow is blocked or the filter needs washing (or the battery is not making contact); it is protection, not a fault in itself. It would be worth a closer look if it still pulses with clear airways, a clean dry filter and a charged battery. Detach the wand and floorhead and look through each part, and check the bin inlet — a coin dropped through the wand should fall straight out. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is a hose split, or was it all clear?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — A vacuum that pulses or cuts out after running is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage starving the airflow — check and clear those before suspecting battery, charger or motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. no burning smell or heat or anything. i emptied the bin, was full of dog hair, still pulsin tho. what next

From what you have described, the most likely cause is a blockage in the hose, wand or floorhead. A jammed brush bar can also make it cut in and out. Turn the floorhead over, clear any hair or thread from the brush bar (roller) and check it turns freely by hand. Was it jammed or tangled (and is it clear now), is it broken, or did it turn freely?
bit of hair on the brush bar, cut it off. still pulsin tho i think

Pulsing on and off is usually the vacuum protecting itself because the airflow is restricted. With it switched off (battery out or unplugged), empty the bin, then wash the filters in cold water and let them dry fully for at least 24 hours — a filter that is even slightly damp causes pulsing. Was a filter clogged or damp (and is it sorted), is a filter damaged, or were they clean and dry already?
uh never washed it, didnt know u could. its grey not purple lol. ok il wash it n leave it overnight

From what you have described, the most likely cause is clogged or damp filters. Clogged filters make the motor work harder and run the battery down faster. Wash them in cold water and let them dry fully (24 hours). Were the filters clogged (and are they clean now), or were they clean already?
washed it, water came out black. left it overnight on the radiator side. pulses way less but still a bit
From what you have described, the most likely cause is a blockage in the hose, wand or floorhead. Charge it fully and use it on the normal mode. Is it running for its normal time now, or still short?
its charged. still pulses a bit tho, not running normal yet. what else should i check

You've already covered the usual blockages well, and the black water from the filter shows that was a big part of it. The next thing to pin down is which power mode you've been running it on, as that changes what the remaining pulsing points to. Boost or max mode drains a cordless battery in a few minutes — that's normal. Was it on boost / max mode (and have you switched to normal), or was it already on the normal mode?
not sure what mode its on, how do i tell? just been holding the trigger. any other bits to check?

The V8 has a small switch on top of the main body, near the handle, that turns MAX (boost) mode on or off, so its position tells you which mode you're in. The next bit to check is the charger and its contacts, as set out below. Check the charger is in a working socket and pushed fully into the vacuum (or dock), and wipe the charging contacts clean and dry. The charging light should come on. Was the charger, socket or contacts the problem (and is it sorted), does the charging light never come on, or is the charger fine with the light on?
charger is fine, it charges up to the 3 blue lights ok. motor runs, just still pulses a bit. what else

Honestly, there isn't much more you can safely check yourself: you've already covered the usual causes of pulsing (the bin, brush bar, filter and charging). Because it still pulses after all of those, the remaining possibilities need proper testing. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
